column2:
radiant(adj./n.)容光煥發的、燦爛的、輻射的、發光體
radiance(n.)光輝、容光煥發
a radiant smile 燦爛的笑容
radiant energy 輻射能
The bride looked radiant in her white wedding dress.
(新娘穿著白色婚紗，看起來容光煥發。)
She greeted every guest with a radiant smile.
(她以燦爛的笑容迎接每一位賓客。)

radiate(v./adj.)散發、輻射、放射狀的
radiation(n.)輻射
radiator(n.)暖氣片、散熱器
radiate heat 散發熱
radiate confidence 散發自信
The stove radiated enough heat to warm the whole room.
(火爐散發的熱足以讓整個房間暖和起來。)
The new captain radiated confidence as she led the team onto the field.
(新隊長帶領隊伍上場時散發著自信。)

radioactive(adj.)放射性的、有輻射的
radioactivity(n.)放射性
radioactive waste 核廢料
radioactive material 放射性物質
Storing radioactive waste safely is a serious problem for many countries.
(安全貯存核廢料是許多國家面臨的嚴重問題。)
Workers must wear protective suits when handling radioactive materials.
(工人處理放射性物質時必須穿防護衣。)

radish(n.)蘿蔔、小紅蘿蔔
(無詞性變化)
white radish 白蘿蔔
radish cake 蘿蔔糕
Radish cake is a popular dish during the Lunar New Year in Taiwan.
(蘿蔔糕是臺灣農曆新年期間很受歡迎的料理。)
My grandmother grows white radishes in her backyard garden.
(我奶奶在後院菜園裡種白蘿蔔。)

radius(n.)半徑、範圍
radii(n.)半徑(複數)
within a radius of 在…半徑範圍內
the radius of a circle 圓的半徑
There are five convenience stores within a radius of one kilometer.
(方圓一公里內有五家便利商店。)
To find the area of a circle, you need to know its radius.
(要算出圓的面積，你需要知道它的半徑。)

rap(n.)饒舌音樂、敲擊聲、責備
rapper(n.)饒舌歌手
rap music 饒舌音樂
a rap on the door 敲門聲
Rap music became popular among young people in the 1990s.
(饒舌音樂在1990年代開始受到年輕人歡迎。)
We heard a sharp rap on the door late at night.
(深夜我們聽到一陣急促的敲門聲。)

rash(n./adj.)疹子、輕率的、魯莽的
rashly(adv.)輕率地
skin rash 皮疹
a rash decision 輕率的決定
Don't make a rash decision when you are angry.
(生氣時不要做出輕率的決定。)
She developed a red rash after eating seafood.
(她吃了海鮮後起了紅疹。)

ratify(v.)批准、正式認可
ratification(n.)批准
ratify a treaty 批准條約
ratify an agreement 批准協議
Both countries must ratify the treaty before it can take effect.
(兩國都必須批准該條約，條約才能生效。)
The agreement was ratified by the legislature last week.
(該協議上週已由立法機關批准。)

realization(n.)領悟、認識、實現
realize(v.)了解、實現
come to the realization 逐漸領悟
the realization of a dream 夢想的實現
He came to the realization that health is more important than money.
(他逐漸領悟到健康比金錢更重要。)
Opening her own bakery was the realization of a lifelong dream.
(開一家自己的麵包店是她畢生夢想的實現。)

reap(v.)收割、收穫、獲得
(無詞性變化)
reap the benefits 獲得好處
reap what you sow 種瓜得瓜、自食其果
Students who study regularly will reap the benefits at exam time.
(平時規律念書的學生在考試時就會嚐到甜頭。)
As the saying goes, you reap what you sow.
(俗話說，種什麼因就得什麼果。)

reckless(adj.)魯莽的、不顧後果的
recklessly(adv.)魯莽地
recklessness(n.)魯莽
reckless driving 魯莽駕駛
reckless behavior 不顧後果的行為
Reckless driving is one of the main causes of traffic accidents.
(魯莽駕駛是交通事故的主要原因之一。)
He spent his money recklessly and soon had nothing left.
(他揮霍無度，很快就一無所有。)

reckon(v.)認為、估計、計算
reckoning(n.)計算、清算
reckon on 指望…
reckon with 處理、對付
I reckon it will take about two hours to get there.
(我估計到那裡大約要兩個小時。)
Do you reckon he will accept our invitation?
(你認為他會接受我們的邀請嗎？)

reconcile(v.)使和解、調和、使接受
reconciliation(n.)和解、調和
reconcile with 與…和解
be reconciled to 勉強接受…
After years of silence, the two brothers finally reconciled.
(經過多年不說話，兩兄弟終於和解了。)
It is hard to reconcile a busy career with family life.
(要兼顧忙碌的工作和家庭生活很困難。)

recreational(adj.)娛樂的、休閒的
recreation(n.)娛樂、消遣
recreational activities 休閒活動
recreational facilities 休閒設施
The park offers many recreational activities such as cycling and fishing.
(這座公園提供許多休閒活動，例如騎單車和釣魚。)
The new community center includes a pool and other recreational facilities.
(新的社區中心包括泳池和其他休閒設施。)

redundancy(n.)多餘、冗詞、裁員
redundant(adj.)多餘的、被裁員的
avoid redundancy 避免贅字
be made redundant 被裁員
Good writers avoid redundancy and choose their words carefully.
(好的作家會避免贅字並謹慎選擇用詞。)
Hundreds of workers were made redundant when the factory closed.
(工廠關閉時，數百名員工被裁員。)

reef(n.)礁、暗礁
(無詞性變化)
coral reef 珊瑚礁
Great Barrier Reef 大堡礁
Coral reefs are home to thousands of species of marine life.
(珊瑚礁是數千種海洋生物的家。)
Rising ocean temperatures are damaging the Great Barrier Reef.
(海水溫度上升正在破壞大堡礁。)

referee(n./v.)裁判、擔任裁判
(無詞性變化)
football referee 足球裁判
referee a match 擔任比賽裁判
The referee blew the whistle to end the first half.
(裁判吹哨結束上半場。)
My uncle has refereed basketball games for over twenty years.
(我舅舅擔任籃球比賽裁判已經二十多年了。)

referendum(n.)公民投票、公投
(無詞性變化)
hold a referendum 舉行公投
a referendum on 針對…的公投
The country held a referendum on whether to change its energy policy.
(該國針對是否改變能源政策舉行了公投。)
The result of the referendum surprised many political experts.
(公投結果讓許多政治專家感到意外。)

refine(v.)精煉、改善、使優雅、refinement(n.)精煉、改進、優雅
refined(adj.)精煉的、有教養的
refinery(n.)精煉廠
refined sugar 精製糖
refine one's skills 精進技巧
She spent months refining her speech for the competition.
(她花了好幾個月修改她的比賽演講稿。)
Eating too much refined sugar is bad for your teeth.
(吃太多精製糖對牙齒不好。)

reflective(adj.)反射的、沉思的、反映…的
reflect(v.)反射、反映、反省
reflection(n.)倒影、反省
reflective vest 反光背心
in a reflective mood 陷入沉思
Road workers must wear reflective vests at night.
(道路工人晚上必須穿反光背心。)
After the trip, she was in a quiet and reflective mood.
(旅行結束後，她安靜地陷入沉思。)

refresh(v.)使恢復精神、更新、refreshment(n.)恢復精神、提神物
refreshing(adj.)令人神清氣爽的
refresh one's memory 喚起記憶
refresh the page 重新整理頁面
A short nap will refresh you after a long morning of classes.
(上了一早上的課後，小睡一下能讓你恢復精神。)
Let me refresh your memory about what we discussed last week.
(讓我幫你回想一下我們上週討論的內容。)

refreshment(n.)恢復精神、提神物、refreshments(n.)茶點、點心飲料
refresh(v.)使恢復精神
light refreshments 簡單的茶點
serve refreshments 供應茶點
Light refreshments will be served after the lecture.
(演講結束後將供應簡單的茶點。)
The hikers stopped at a small shop for some refreshment.
(登山客在一家小店停下來稍作休息、吃點東西。)

refute(v.)反駁、駁斥
refutation(n.)反駁
refute a claim 駁斥說法
refute an argument 反駁論點
The scientist used new data to refute the old theory.
(那位科學家用新數據駁斥了舊理論。)
The company quickly refuted the rumors about its financial problems.
(公司迅速駁斥了有關其財務問題的謠言。)

rehabilitate(v.)使康復、使恢復正常生活、修復
rehabilitation(n.)復健、康復、修復
rehabilitation center 復健中心
rehabilitate patients 使病人康復
The program helps rehabilitate injured athletes so they can compete again.
(這項計畫協助受傷的運動員復健，讓他們能再次參賽。)
After the surgery, he needed months of rehabilitation to walk normally.
(手術後，他需要好幾個月的復健才能正常走路。)

rehearse(v.)排練、預演
rehearsal(n.)排練、彩排
dress rehearsal 彩排
rehearse a play 排練戲劇
The drama club rehearsed the play every afternoon for a month.
(戲劇社一個月來每天下午都在排練這齣戲。)
We had a dress rehearsal the day before the graduation ceremony.
(畢業典禮的前一天我們進行了彩排。)

reign(n./v.)統治時期、統治、盛行
(無詞性變化)
during the reign of 在…統治期間
reign supreme 居於首位
Many great buildings were built during the reign of Queen Victoria.
(許多宏偉的建築是在維多利亞女王統治期間建造的。)
Silence reigned in the classroom after the teacher's announcement.
(老師宣布之後，教室裡一片寂靜。)

rejoice(v.)欣喜、高興
rejoicing(n.)歡騰、喜悅
rejoice at/over 為…感到欣喜
rejoice in 樂於…
The whole town rejoiced at the news of the team's victory.
(全鎮都為球隊獲勝的消息而歡欣鼓舞。)
Fans rejoiced in the streets after the national team won the championship.
(國家隊奪冠後，球迷們在街頭歡慶。)

relay(n./v.)接力賽、轉達、轉播
(無詞性變化)
relay race 接力賽
relay a message 轉達訊息
Our class won first place in the 400-meter relay race.
(我們班在四百公尺接力賽中得到第一名。)
Please relay this message to the rest of the team.
(請把這則訊息轉達給隊上其他人。)

relentless(adj.)不懈的、無情的、持續不斷的
relentlessly(adv.)不停地、無情地
relentless pressure 持續不斷的壓力
relentless pursuit 不懈的追求
The relentless rain caused flooding in several parts of the city.
(持續不斷的大雨導致城市多處淹水。)
Her relentless pursuit of excellence made her a top athlete.
(她對卓越的不懈追求使她成為頂尖運動員。)

reliance(n.)依賴、信賴
rely(v.)依賴
reliant(adj.)依賴的
reliance on 對…的依賴
heavy reliance 嚴重依賴
The country is trying to reduce its reliance on imported oil.
(該國正試圖減少對進口石油的依賴。)
Too much reliance on smartphones may affect our ability to concentrate.
(過度依賴智慧型手機可能影響我們的專注力。)

reliant(adj.)依賴的、依靠的
reliance(n.)依賴
self-reliant(adj.)自立的
be reliant on 依賴…
heavily reliant 高度依賴
The island is heavily reliant on tourism for its income.
(這座島的收入高度依賴觀光業。)
Living alone taught him to become more self-reliant.
(獨自生活讓他學會更加自立。)

relic(n.)遺物、遺跡、遺俗
(無詞性變化)
ancient relics 古代遺物
a relic of the past 過去的遺物
The museum displays relics from the Ming Dynasty.
(這座博物館展出明朝的文物。)
The old typewriter is a relic of a time before computers.
(這台舊打字機是電腦問世之前的時代遺物。)

remainder(n.)剩餘部分、餘數
remain(v.)剩下、保持
remaining(adj.)剩餘的
the remainder of 其餘的…
for the remainder of 在…剩下的時間
She spent the remainder of her vacation reading at home.
(她把剩下的假期都用來在家看書。)
When you divide 10 by 3, the remainder is 1.
(當你把十除以三時，餘數是一。)

reminiscent(adj.)使人聯想起的、懷舊的
reminisce(v.)追憶、緬懷
reminiscence(n.)回憶
be reminiscent of 讓人想起…
reminisce about 回憶…
The taste of this soup is reminiscent of my mother's cooking.
(這碗湯的味道讓我想起媽媽的手藝。)
The old classmates spent the evening reminiscing about their school days.
(老同學們整晚都在回憶學生時代。)

renowned(adj.)著名的、有聲譽的
renown(n.)名聲、聲望
be renowned for 以…聞名
world-renowned 世界知名的
Taiwan is renowned for its delicious street food.
(臺灣以美味的街頭小吃聞名。)
The concert featured a world-renowned violinist from Germany.
(這場音樂會邀請了一位來自德國的世界知名小提琴家。)

reproduce(v.)繁殖、複製、再現
reproduction(n.)繁殖、複製品
reproductive(adj.)生殖的
reproduce quickly 快速繁殖
reproduce a painting 複製畫作
Rabbits can reproduce very quickly if they are not controlled.
(如果不加以控制，兔子可以繁殖得非常快。)
The painting in the hotel lobby is a reproduction of a famous work.
(飯店大廳的那幅畫是一幅名作的複製品。)

reptile(n./adj.)爬蟲類動物、爬蟲類的
reptilian(adj.)爬蟲類的
reptile house 爬蟲館
cold-blooded reptiles 冷血的爬蟲類
Snakes, lizards, and turtles are all reptiles.
(蛇、蜥蜴和烏龜都是爬蟲類。)
Reptiles often lie in the sun to warm their bodies.
(爬蟲類常躺在陽光下讓身體變暖。)

resent(v.)憤恨、怨恨、resentment(n.)憤恨、怨恨
resentful(adj.)憤恨的
resent being 對被…感到不滿
feel resentment toward 對…感到怨恨
Teenagers often resent being treated like little children.
(青少年常常不滿被當成小孩對待。)
Unfair treatment can create deep resentment among employees.
(不公平的待遇可能在員工之間造成很深的怨恨。)

reside(v.)居住、存在於
residence(n.)住所、居住
resident(n.)居民
reside in 居住在…
permanent residence 永久居留
Most of his relatives now reside in Kaohsiung.
(他大部分的親戚現在住在高雄。)
Local residents complained about the noise from the new factory.
(當地居民抱怨新工廠的噪音。)

resistant(adj.)抵抗的、有抵抗力的、耐…的
resist(v.)抵抗
resistance(n.)抵抗、抵抗力
water-resistant 防水的
resistant to 對…有抵抗力
This watch is water-resistant up to fifty meters.
(這支錶可防水至五十公尺。)
Some bacteria have become resistant to common antibiotics.
(有些細菌已對常見的抗生素產生抗藥性。)

respective(adj.)分別的、各自的
respectively(adv.)分別地、各自地
their respective homes 他們各自的家
respective fields 各自的領域
After the party, the guests returned to their respective homes.
(派對結束後，賓客們各自回家。)
Tom and Mary scored 85 and 92 points respectively.
(湯姆和瑪莉分別得了85分和92分。)

restoration(n.)恢復、修復、重建
restore(v.)恢復、修復
restoration work 修復工程
the restoration of 某事物的恢復
The restoration of the old temple took nearly three years.
(這座古廟的修復花了將近三年。)
Everyone welcomed the restoration of electricity after the typhoon.
(颱風過後電力恢復，大家都很高興。)

restrain(v.)抑制、克制、阻止
restraint(n.)克制、約束
restrain oneself 克制自己
restrain sb. from 阻止某人做…
She could hardly restrain her excitement when she heard the news.
(聽到這個消息時，她幾乎無法抑制自己的興奮。)
The police had to restrain the angry man from attacking others.
(警方必須制止那名憤怒的男子攻擊他人。)

restraint(n.)克制、節制、約束
restrain(v.)抑制
show restraint 表現克制
without restraint 毫無節制地
Both sides were asked to show restraint and avoid violence.
(雙方都被要求保持克制、避免暴力。)
Children in cars must be secured with proper safety restraints.
(車內的孩童必須用適當的安全裝置固定。)

retort(n./v.)反駁、回嘴
(無詞性變化)
a sharp retort 尖銳的反駁
retort angrily 憤怒地反駁
'It's none of your business,' she retorted angrily.
(「不關你的事。」她憤怒地反駁。)
His clever retort made the whole class laugh.
(他機智的回嘴讓全班哄堂大笑。)

retrieve(v.)取回、找回、檢索
retrieval(n.)取回、檢索
retrieve data 擷取資料
information retrieval 資訊檢索
I managed to retrieve the lost files from my old computer.
(我設法從舊電腦中找回了遺失的檔案。)
The dog ran into the lake to retrieve the ball.
(那隻狗跑進湖裡把球叼回來。)

revelation(n.)揭露、透露、啟示
reveal(v.)揭露、透露
a shocking revelation 驚人的揭露
come as a revelation 令人大開眼界
The revelation that the mayor had lied shocked the public.
(市長說謊一事被揭露後震驚了大眾。)
Visiting the science museum was a revelation for the young students.
(參觀科學博物館讓年輕學生大開眼界。)

revival(n.)復甦、復興、重新流行
revive(v.)使復甦
economic revival 經濟復甦
a revival of interest 重新引起興趣
There has been a revival of interest in vinyl records among young people.
(年輕人對黑膠唱片重新燃起興趣。)
The government hopes the new policy will lead to an economic revival.
(政府希望新政策能帶動經濟復甦。)

revive(v.)使甦醒、使復活、使復興
revival(n.)復甦、復興
revive the economy 振興經濟
revive a tradition 恢復傳統
The doctors managed to revive the man who had stopped breathing.
(醫生們成功救醒了那名停止呼吸的男子。)
The village is trying to revive its traditional festivals to attract tourists.
(這個村莊正努力恢復傳統節慶來吸引觀光客。)

revolt(n./v.)反叛、起義、使反感
revolting(adj.)令人作嘔的
rise in revolt 起義
revolt against 反抗…
The farmers rose in revolt against the unfair taxes.
(農民們起義反抗不公平的稅收。)
The smell of the rotten fish was absolutely revolting.
(腐爛的魚的味道令人極度作嘔。)

revolve(v.)旋轉、繞轉、以…為中心
revolution(n.)革命、公轉
revolving(adj.)旋轉的
revolve around 繞著…轉、以…為中心
revolving door 旋轉門
The earth revolves around the sun once a year.
(地球每年繞太陽公轉一圈。)
Her whole life seems to revolve around her children.
(她整個生活似乎都圍繞著她的孩子打轉。)

rigorous(adj.)嚴格的、嚴謹的、嚴酷的
rigorously(adv.)嚴格地
rigor(n.)嚴格、嚴謹
rigorous training 嚴格的訓練
rigorous testing 嚴格的測試
Astronauts must go through years of rigorous training.
(太空人必須經過多年嚴格的訓練。)
All new medicines undergo rigorous testing before they are sold.
(所有新藥在上市前都要經過嚴格的測試。)

ripple(n./v.)漣漪、波紋、起漣漪
(無詞性變化)
ripple effect 連鎖效應
a ripple of laughter 一陣笑聲
The stone created small ripples on the surface of the pond.
(石頭在池塘水面上激起小小的漣漪。)
